text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — noticed a gap in admission observability this morning. Some tenants spiked token shapes (lots of short, high-QPS requests) and the admission layer silently degraded them without clear metric attribution. Anyone seen this pattern?
Alex Chen: Yep saw errors in the gateway trace, but admission spans only show accept/reject, not the token-shape buckets. hard to tell if it was kv-cache pressure vs smoothing.
Kevin O'Leary: I think the smoothing window kicked in because of bursty per-second tokens. We don't emit per-tenant token_histogram in the admission path right now (only at the edge).
Maya Patel: Exact problem: customer complained about increased 503s even though overall capacity unused. Diagnosis showed many small requests hitting hot KV shards; admission backoff took effect based on cumulative credits. No clear link in logs.
Sasha Ivanov: Proposal: add an admission-level metric: admit_token_shape{tenant,shape=short|long,count,median_size} + admit_cause{tenant,reason}. That way we can join with kv-cache eviction rates.
Alex Chen: +1 on shape metrics. Tradeoff: cardinality explosion if we tag too many dimensions. Keep shapes coarse (short/medium/long) and bucket sizes.
Kevin O'Leary: Also need tracing: instrument admission decision with a small payload (counts and chosen penalty). Example span payload: 
```
admit.decision: {"action":"defer","penalty_ms":120,"token_shape":"short","recent_qps":320}
```
Maya Patel: That looks good. Privacy/compliance check: ensure no prompt text flows into telemetry. Only counts and sizes.
Sasha Ivanov: Agree. Also suggest a synthetic probe for the admission circuit: periodic low-priority probe that logs observed admit path latency and outcome per-tenant. Helps detect silent degradations.
Alex Chen: Operationally we'll need a fast dashboard: per-tenant admit success %, admit_latency p50/p95, token_shape distribution, kv_cache_evictions/s. Can we reuse current edge metrics pipeline? Might need an ingest QOS for high-card tenants.
Kevin O'Leary: Implementation note: push metrics from the local admit sidecar (low overhead counter rings) every 10s. If we try to stream every request it'll blow up. Use delta counters.
Maya Patel: Action items: 1) Sasha to draft metric names and shapes (by EOD) 2) Alex to prototype trace payloads in local admit sidecar 3) Kevin to add a short-run dashboard and link to incident runbook.
Sasha Ivanov: I'll post a concise RFC snippet in #eng-platform when done. Will include a sample Grafana panel and alert thresholds (eg: admit_failure_rate > 1% sustained 60s + token_shape_short_ratio > 0.6).
deploy-bot: Deployed: admit-sidecar v0.9.2 with no-op tracing hooks to staging.
Maya Patel: Great. One more thought — we should map admit_cause labels to SLO impacts (ex: "kv_pressure" -> increase probe weight). That will let Optimize recommend quantization or caching tweaks for affected tenants.
Alex Chen: True. Add an enum for cause so downstream tooling can consume it.
Kevin O'Leary: I'll mock a sample log join query we can run: 
```
SELECT t.tenant_id, sum(a.rejected) as rejects, avg(a.penalty_ms) as avg_penalty, sum(k.evictions) as evictions
FROM admit_metrics a JOIN kv_metrics k USING (tenant_id, floor(ts/60))
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY rejects DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Maya Patel: Nice. If everyone is aligned I'll move this into a follow-up RFC for admission observability tweaks + an implementation checklist. Thanks all :rocket:
